en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Names of One Hundred Buddhas, translated by the Tripitaka Master Narendrayaśas of India during the Sui Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.

He was surrounded before and behind by a great assembly of hundreds of thousands of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, as well as a multitude of great bodhisattvas, and the great deva kings Śakra, Mahābrahmā, and the Four Great Kings, along with devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, who paid him homage, made offerings, revered him, and praised him.
At that time, the World-Honored One was proclaiming the sublime Dharma for the great assembly.

Then, the Venerable Śāriputra rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, knelt with his right knee on the ground, pressed his ten fingers together in palms-joined reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will proclaim the names of the Buddhas currently residing in the worlds of the ten directions."

Why is this? If there are sons or daughters of good family who hear the names of these present Buddhas, they will generate great merit, resolve their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, attain non-retrogression, and shall also swiftly achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra: “Excellent, excellent!

It is because you now desire to bring benefit, peace, and happiness to the great assembly; because you wish to protect and have compassion for all sentient beings; because you wish to fulfill the aspirations of all sentient beings; because you desire to cause all to give rise to joy; and also because you wish to increase the roots of goodness for all future bodhisattvas—excellent, excellent!”
— Having given rise to wholesome thoughts and reflections, he asked such questions.
That he asked such questions was entirely through the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata, Śāriputra!

Listen attentively now! If there are sons or daughters of good family who, upon hearing the names of these present Buddhas, are able to receive and uphold them, all hosts of Māras shall find no opportunity against such persons, nor shall any evil people find an opportunity. They shall obtain immeasurable, boundless, and profound merit; wherever they are born, they shall be endowed with the practices of a bodhisattva and attain the supernormal power of recollecting past lives. Their countenances shall be upright and their various marks complete; they shall always be able to draw near to and make offerings to all Buddhas, until they swiftly achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Why is this? Śāriputra!

If there are those who hear the names of these Buddhas, uphold, read, recite, reverently prostrate to, transcribe, make offerings to, and successively teach them to others, the merit they obtain will be immeasurable and boundless.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"If one can uphold the names of these Buddhas, this person shall not be wounded by blades;
poisons cannot harm them, fire cannot burn them, and they shall not fall into the eight difficult states."
Having beheld the golden light of great wisdom, the Kings of Dharma endowed with the thirty-two marks,
and having thus seen those Buddhas, they made immeasurable offerings to them.
Their eyes are neither blind nor reddish-yellow; their bodies are not hunched or crooked, nor are they one-eyed.
They attain a body of great power like that of Nārāyaṇa—such is the retribution for upholding the name of the Buddha.
They shall always receive offerings from devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and others;
enemies and wicked people cannot harm them—such is the retribution for upholding the name of the Buddha.
Listen attentively now, Śāriputra!
According to these subtle and wondrous words spoken by me, whoever hears the names of these Buddhas shall draw near to the path of enlightenment.
Therefore, listen now with a sincere heart: The Great Dharma King of the worlds of the ten directions,
Who can pull out the thorns of affliction for sentient beings, Like a medicinal tree that eliminates all maladies,
Bestows upon the ignorant, blind, and deluded ordinary people The eye of wisdom of a Bodhisattva.
Furthermore, suppose there were a supreme Bodhisattva who practiced giving, filling worlds as numerous as the sands of immeasurable billions of Ganges Rivers with Jambūnada gold,
and offered it to the Great Teacher of Great Compassion without ceasing throughout the six periods of the day and night; [the merit of this would not equal that of one who hears this Dharma].
With banners, canopies, and robes as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, one might practice giving with a single-minded focus throughout immeasurable thousands of millions of billions of kalpas;
or one might erect Buddha-stūpas filling the entire world and make offerings to them for ten kalpas.
As many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges;
their stupas are all made of the seven precious jewels, filling ten thousand lands in this manner,
numbering thirty-six billion, fashioned from red sandalwood and pearls.

They fashioned parasols as objects of worship, each individual parasol able to cover entirely all lands equal to a hundred buddha-worlds; with pearls and tassels reaching to the limits of the buddha-fields,
their number being like the sands of the Ganges, they further fashioned golden parasols in the sky.
Their number is likewise like the sands of the Ganges; their color is like that of a statue of refined purple-gold.
Each one shines universally throughout the three thousandfold world-systems, and within each and every stupa, offerings are made for immeasurable, boundless, and countless eons.
All the merits performed as described above do not equal the power of being able to resolve upon bodhicitta.
Likewise, being able to resolve upon bodhicitta and abiding in heedfulness and pure precepts does not equal the power of being able to uphold the names of these Buddhas.
Thus, those who can uphold the names of these Buddhas, and who moreover feel compassion for all sentient beings,
causing [these names] to spread widely in every direction and instructing others to receive and uphold them—
among all sentient beings, they shall act as a field of merit just like the Tathāgata.
At that time, the Buddha told Śāriputra:

"If there is one who single-mindedly upholds, recites, and remembers without forgetting the names of these Buddhas, the greed, anger, ignorance, and all fears that have already arisen will be extinguished, and those greed, anger, ignorance, and fears that have not yet arisen will be prevented from arising."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke the names of the Buddhas:
"Namo Candraprabha Buddha; Namo Akṣobhya Buddha."

Homage to the Buddha Nāgarakṣitaparitrāyaka. "The names of these Buddhas and others are able to protect and deliver the world."
Recite once during the first watch of the night, And sleep while keeping the Buddha in mind;
Recite once during the middle watch, And likewise during the final watch.
In this manner, throughout the three periods of the day— The first, middle, and final divisions—
Recite this once at a time, with diligence and without negligence.
Because of reciting these names of the Buddhas, one will always have auspicious dreams;
evil spirits and wicked people shall find no opportunity to cause harm.
Therefore, this name of the Buddha is able to protect and deliver the world;
no celestial musicians, spirits, yakṣas, kumbhāṇḍas, rākṣasas,
or any other ghosts and deities can raise obstacles.
Those who are able to constantly recollect and uphold these names of one hundred Buddhas,
no demonic activities whatsoever will be able to find an opportunity against them.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and the kings of the Heaven of the Thirty-three...
Adjusting his robes and sitting with knees bent and palms joined,
he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
Those who uphold the names of the Buddhas, as well as the Four Great Heavenly Kings,
shall also constantly protect them— those who uphold the names of the Buddhas.
Except for those with karma that is fixed and inevitable, which cannot be saved or protected.
Among all devas and humans, none are able to inflict harm.
At that time, the All-Knowing One uttered a great and subtle voice,
an eightfold melody of harmony and elegance, beautiful and pleasing for all to hear.
He universally addressed the great assembly:
"Throughout the worlds of the ten directions, may this be widely disseminated everywhere,
performing a great Dharma-giving and severing the doubts of sentient beings."
When the Great Sage Śākyamuni expounded this Dharma,
three hundred bhikṣus all attained the exhaustion of all outflows; furthermore, there were forty bhikṣuṇīs.
All outflows exhausted, they attained arhatship;
furthermore, there were five thousand upāsakas who,
dwelling in a state of supreme joy, realized the fruit of srotāpanna.
Furthermore, there were one thousand one hundred upāsikās,
all of whom had distanced themselves from dust and defilement and attained the purity of the Dharma-eye;
there were also great celestial kings with immeasurable thousands of millions of followers.
Within the Dharma of the Dharma King, they have attained the pure Dharma-eye;
like the sands of the Ganges, divided into three parts,
the Bodhisattvas constitute one part, all of whom have attained the patience of non-arising.
At that time, the three thousandfold great thousandfold world-system shook in six ways;
the mountains and lofty peaks, and the entire great earth, all roared with tremors.
In the sky above, a rain of various celestial, wondrous flowers fell.
The joyful sounds of devas, nāgas, non-humans, and others completely filled [the air].
At that time, Śakra-devendra, Maudgalyāyana, Revata, Sarpadāsa, Kapphiṇa, and Mahākātyāyana—
As well as Mahākāśyapa, Uruvilvākāśyapa, and even Nāgakāśyapa, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra, Subhūti, Adarśanakaśyapa, Ānanda, and Bhadrika.
Dravyamāla-putra and the rest of this great assembly—
twenty-five thousand people in all— in unison addressed the Buddha, saying: “O Dharma King,
Lion of the Śākyas, we shall exert the full power of our diligence.”
Without exception, through the power of various supernormal faculties,
they manifest infinite bodies throughout immeasurable worlds;
passing beyond countless Buddha-fields, they constantly proclaim the names of these Buddhas.
Just as the Buddha has taught,
in order to cause the assembly to see, he manifested great supernormal powers;
through the Buddha’s power of spiritual penetration, he revealed immeasurable billions of lands.
Beholding the Lion-King of the Śākyas, who is omnipresent everywhere,
preaching this sūtra; it is no different from what was taught by the Buddhas of the past.
The Buddha addressed the great assembly:
"Throughout immeasurable kalpas, I have long skillfully cultivated supernormal powers;
regarding this unsurpassed Buddha-dharma, you must certainly not give rise to doubt."
"For the sake of bringing peace and security to sentient beings, quickly recite these names of the Buddhas,
so that all sentient beings alike may forever be free from the suffering of birth and death.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Śāriputra:

“If there are good men or good women who, having heard the names of these Buddhas, develop deep and pure faith, resolve their minds on Bodhi, joyfully accept and uphold [these names], and practice with diligence day and night—reading, reciting, copying, and widely explaining them to others—they shall attain immeasurable, boundless, and vast merit; they shall never regress and shall swiftly achieve Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, such that no demons whatsoever can disturb or confuse them.”

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the Venerable Śāriputra, Śakra, Brahmā, and the Four Heavenly Kings, along with the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, and the entire great assembly, having heard this Dharma, were all filled with great joy.
